what_this_is: The numbers behind the rules. Every value was measured in pixels from the reference material; the source is named for each one.

gutter_px.where: between every two blocks, in all three lcarsde screenshots
gutter_px.note: the widest gutter measured is 10px, at the elbow of a block; the plain gap is 8px

cell_thickness_px.where: the cells of the application menu

elbow_radius_px.where: the rounded end of a 40px cell
elbow_radius_px.note: one rounded end only, radius = half the thickness

frame_edge_px.where: the segments of the right frame edge

status_cell_width_px.where: the coloured cells of the lcarsde status bar
status_cell_width_px.note: the black areas between them are the text

black_gutter.note: black is the gutter and the field, never a background behind a block

palette.source: read out of the lcarsde screenshots; these are the canonical LCARS colours

the_frame_parts.title: one line of large right-aligned type, above everything
the_frame_parts.readout_field: a field of right-aligned digits, in rows; the numbers are the content
the_frame_parts.nav: four buttons, always at the top right
the_frame_parts.spine: a stack of tall blocks on the left edge
the_frame_parts.window: the reading area; its title bar sits BELOW it (lcarsde manual)
the_frame_parts.edge: a strip of 31px segments closing the frame on the right

components.name: .lcars-text-bar
components.what: a bar with the heading knocked out in black

components.name: .lcars-list
components.what: a list, each row with an ellipse marker 34x18

components.name: .flexbox / .col
components.what: two columns that wrap on narrow screens

components.name: .image-frame
components.what: a picture in a frame with a five-block base

components.name: .data-cascade
components.what: a grid of digits whose colour cycles in groups

the_motion.readout_colour_cycle: the digit rows cycle their colour in groups (data-group-1/1a/2/2b/3) every 6s - the layout never moves
the_motion.press_feedback: a panel answers a press with brightness, and the frame segment next to it answers too (the template does it with :has())
the_motion.value_change: a changed value rolls or flips; it never fades in
